entities.summary: Lake Ilopango is a crater lake which fills an 8 by 11 km: 70.5 km2 (27.2 sq mi) volcanic caldera in central El Salvador, on the borders of the San Salvador, La Paz, and Cuscatlán departments. The caldera, which contains the second largest lake in the country and is immediately east of the capital city, San Salvador, has a scalloped 100 m (330 ft) to 500 m (1,600 ft) high rim. Any surplus drains via the Jiboa River to the Pacific Ocean. The local military airbase, Ilopango International Airport, has annual airshows where international pilots from all over the world fly over San Salvador City and Ilopango lake.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Lake Ilopango's formation around 450 AD had a significant impact on the region, as it became an important site for the Mayan civilization and later influenced the development of the Aztec Empire. The lake's unique geology also made it a crucial location for trade and commerce.
